macro_cross_check.verdict: PROTEIN GAP EXCEEDS THE 15% INSTRUMENT AND IS EXPLAINED, NOT A PORTION ERROR. The main protein is weight-anchored (1.25 lb printed; our only drift is +2.9% quantization, which pushes our protein UP, the wrong direction to create this gap). Rebuilding OUR EXACT line set with the 99/1 Ground Turkey label row (120 cal / 26 P / 1.5 F per 112 g) in place of 93/7 reproduces the source's published figures almost exactly: 427.4 cal (-1.3%), 37.7 P (-0.7%), 22.3 F (-7%), 17.2 C. Their calculator used an extra-lean 99/1-class turkey for the generic phrase 'ground turkey'. The in-run precedent (three recipes, identical phrase) books 93/7, the house label row with a wired bid; 99/1 resolves in the vocab but has NO BID, so booking it would hold the recipe for wiring it has never had. The 93/7 build is internally consistent and is what the card will publish.
macro_cross_check.band_check: computed 492.5 cal in [400, 650] PASS with 92 cal above the floor and 158 below the ceiling; carbs 17.2 g <= 35 PASS. The only >5% drift on a macro-bearing line is the 3.5 -> 4 egg quantization (+2.5 cal/serving).

loud_flags: Protein cross-check gap -17.9% is OUTSIDE the 15% instrument; kept because the identical-basis 99/1 reconstruction pins the entire gap on the source's lean-class assumption (all four macros reconcile within 7% on their basis). The published card will state ~31 g protein where the source page says 38; that is the honest 93/7 figure, but QA should accept the divergence knowingly. If the gate owner prefers the source-matching lean build, the path is wiring a bid for the existing 99/1 Ground Turkey row, not remapping here.

Worcestershire totals 12 1/4 tbsp scaled across the two sections - faithful to the printed 3.5 tbsp per 4 servings, just visually large at 14 servings; flagged for the writer as a cook-note candidate, not changed.
